correctness.rationale: The addition theorem converts evaluation rank to Legendre Gram rank. The exact quadratic-field identity at degree nine produces two independent signed layer annihilators. The standalone standard-library checker directly verifies both and certifies matching lower ranks for every degree 0–119 in two characteristic-prime specializations, whose invertible denominators make a nonzero modular minor a valid characteristic-zero lower bound. Dimension gives all small-degree upper bounds. For all l>=120, DLMF 18.14.7 gives absolute off-diagonal Legendre values below 1/11 and hence strict Hermitian Gram diagonal dominance, proving full rank without extrapolation.

value.rationale: The sample set is the canonical regular rhombicuboctahedral antipodal vertex orbit; individual spherical-harmonic degrees are the natural frequency bands for interpolation. A previously surjective degree-eight band loses an identifiable two-dimensional signed-symmetry mode at degree nine and recovers full interpolation at every subsequent degree. The exact all-degree rank law and explicit missing-data constraints go beyond a cheap low-dimensional dimension count or an unmotivated finite census.
